chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Simṭ, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When the child reaches four months, perform cupping on him every month in the fovea (hollow of the neck/back), for it dries up his saliva and lowers the heat from his head and body.'

key_terms.النُّقْرَة: the fovea/hollow (of the neck or back)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on cupping for infants according to the Imams?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes monthly cupping at the 'nuqrah' (hollow of the neck) for infants from four months to manage excess saliva and reduce bodily heat, reflecting the integration of Prophetic medicine (Tibb al-Nabawi) with clinical observation in Shia jurisprudence. This practice highlights the Shia emphasis on preventive healthcare and the purification of the body as a means to maintain spiritual and physical purity, aligning with the broader tradition of utilizing natural remedies prescribed by the Ahl al-Bayt.
